checked_claims.claim: Import caching guarantees identity across path changes
checked_claims.reason: Cache lookup is name-based, not physical-file global identity; different resolution names may import same file twice. Prepend/append mismatch has documented skips.

material_errors: Cache lookup is name-based, not physical-file global identity; different resolution names may import same file twice. Prepend/append mismatch has documented skips.
tasks.notes: Static inspection of pinned source; no upstream code execution.
tasks.corrected_reference_answer: importlib mode first resolves a package name and checks sys.modules, attempts a spec import, then falls back to a path-derived name with another cache check (src/_pytest/pathlib.py:535-566). It does not scan cached modules by physical path, so changed name resolution can produce separate module objects. prepend/append modes adjust sys.path, import by name, and generally compare __file__ to the requested path; __init__.py returns early and PY_IGNORE_IMPORTMISMATCH=1 disables the check (src/_pytest/pathlib.py:568-612). Repeated identical names reuse the cache; arbitrary sys.path changes do not guarantee physical-file identity.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: pytest_internalerror converts excrepr to text, splits on newline, and prefixes every resulting line with INTERNALERROR> before write_line (src/_pytest/terminal.py:560-563). If the representation were guaranteed to contain no newline, it could instead call self.write_line('INTERNALERROR> ' + str(excrepr)) once and return True, eliminating split and iteration. Keep the loop for the actual potentially multiline representation; no meaningful performance gain is established.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: ensure_deletable returns False for a symlink, catches OSError from lock.is_file and Exception from lock.stat, and otherwise checks expiration (src/_pytest/pathlib.py:310-327). For an expired lock, unlink and return True are both inside suppress(OSError); if unlink raises, execution skips that return and reaches False (src/_pytest/pathlib.py:328-335). A status-check failure returns early before unlink. This contains expected cleanup races conservatively; it is not an absolute promise that every possible exception is caught.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: tmpdir converts the already supplied tmp_path with legacy_path and returns it (src/_pytest/legacypath.py:318-320). This occurs during tmpdir fixture setup after its dependency is resolved. It changes the path API, not the directory allocated upstream. The code has no silent-failure handler: a conversion exception propagates as setup failure. If a hypothetical converter instead returned an invalid value, consumers could fail, but directory reuse or cross-test interference does not follow automatically; that would depend on additional consumer fallback behavior.

tasks.corrected_reference_answer: _try_repr_or_str tries repr and, for ordinary failures, formats a type-named string using the object; control exceptions are reraised (src/_pytest/_io/saferepr.py:7-13). _format_repr_exception catches failure to render the original exception and tries the inner exception under an 'unpresentable exception' label before assembling the placeholder (src/_pytest/_io/saferepr.py:16-25). These layers handle common broken repr/str cases, but do not guarantee success: formatting the inner exception can also fail and is not wrapped in another fallback here.
